Hi Sam —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Per our conversation I attached our standard SLA template (Redwood_SLA_Template_v1.3.pdf) so your procurement and ops teams can review suggested uptime and credit mechanics. High level summary we propose:

- Uptime (global baseline): 99.95% monthly
- Monthly service credits: tiered (partial credit at 99.9-99.95, larger credits below 99.0) — full schedule in the attachment
- Latency SLOs: we call out p95 targets for common workloads (text-gen, chat, embeddings) in the appendix
- Scheduled maintenance: standard clause that scheduled maintenance notified 7 days in advance is not counted as downtime

A couple of things I wanted to flag for NimbleWorks specifically:
- If you expect extended maintenance windows in APAC during your go-live window, we can discuss region-specific uptime baselines or carve-outs.
- If your security/compliance team needs stricter notification windows or audit logs for maintenance, we can include that in the contract language.

Can you confirm who from your procurement and cloud ops teams should be looped in? Also if you have particular latency targets (e.g., embeddings p95 < 100ms) call them out so we can check feasibility for your expected traffic and regions.

If it helps, I can loop in Marcus (product) and Laura (legal) to get quicker alignment on any exceptions.

Thanks,

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the template. Quick notes from our side after a first pass (ops & procurement):

- APAC weekend maintenance windows: our infra team expects occasional rolling node patching that can require up to 6 hours of degraded capacity per week across regions during the first 3 months. That makes a 99.95% APAC baseline hard for our launch.
- Latency: for embeddings (used heavily by search ranking) we are targeting p95 < 120ms; for chat/text-gen we need p95 < 350ms for our 4k workflow. If those are outside normal bounds, we need to negotiate credits or a regional SLA carve-out.
- Notice: procurement requests that scheduled maintenance notifications be 7 business days minimum, with a published maintenance calendar if maintenance is expected more than once per month.

Can Redwood accept a region-specific uptime baseline of 99.5% for APAC for the first 6 months, with a path to 99.95% after that? If so, we can move forward with procurement.

Looping in procurement@nimbleworks.com for visibility.

—Sam

Hi all —

Thanks for flagging the APAC behavior, Sam. Technical takeaways and proposal from product:

1) Latency SLOs
- Embeddings: p95 target 120ms is reasonable for our quantized embedding pipeline in APAC for modest QPS (<50/sec) if using the regional cluster with burst pooling. We will call out p50/p95/p99 in the appendix and bind p95 for contract clarity.
- Text-gen / chat (4k context): p95 < 350ms is achievable for streams under expected batch sizing; longer sequences and high concurrent streams will raise p95. We should include a clause that tail latency may increase with sustained concurrency > X (we can add measured thresholds).

2) APAC uptime baseline exception
- We can accept a region-specific baseline of 99.5% for APAC for an initial 6-month ramp period provided:
  a) Scheduled maintenance windows are calendared and published when recurring (maintenance-calendar.csv).
  b) Scheduled maintenance notified >= 7 business days in advance will not count toward downtime.
  c) Emergency maintenance (security fixes) will be best-effort notification and treated separately; we should limit emergency maintenance to critical patches only.

3) Credits & measurement
- Proposal: credits apply regionally; if APAC falls below 99.5% in a month, credits begin at the same tiered schedule in the template but calculated only against APAC region usage.
- We will add an appendix that defines how we compute region-level uptime and examples for hybrid traffic routing.

Action items:
- Product will draft the technical SLA appendix with concrete p95 numbers and concurrency caveats by Monday.
- Legal to provide redline for the regional exception and emergency maintenance language.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Sam / Soojin / Marcus —

I've attached a redline addressing the APAC exception: SLA_Redline_NimbleWorks_20260215.docx. Key legal points:

- We are prepared to accept a temporary APAC baseline of 99.5% for an initial six-month period. After six months, we will review telemetry and automatically revert the contract baseline to 99.95% unless both parties agree to extend the lower baseline.
- Credits: propose a region-scoped credit schedule (same tiers as global template) but cap total monthly credits at 30% of that region's invoice for severe repeated outages. This protects Redwood from disproportionate exposure while giving NimbleWorks meaningful remediation.
- Scheduled maintenance: will not be counted as downtime if announced >=7 business days and published in the maintenance calendar (maintenance-calendar.csv).
- Emergency maintenance: allow for immediate action with best-effort notification; we will limit invocation to security fixes and high-severity incidents, with a post-incident report and follow-up credit evaluation if appropriate.
- Audit / logs: NimbleWorks requested proof of maintenance notifications and audit trails. We can provide system audit logs and a monthly maintenance digest as an optional add-on.

I'll incorporate Marcus's latency appendix once provided and produce a clean contract doc with the regional carve-out. Attaching redline.

Laura Bennett
